subject: Aurora-6B intermittent response failures — impact update and next steps
messages:

Cc: support@acme-energy.com
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden failures from Aurora-6B since 08:50 UTC

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing a spike of 502/504 responses from requests routed to Aurora-6B at ~08:50 UTC this morning. The errors affected our ingestion pipeline (batch jobs) and a handful of product API calls — roughly 6% of requests returned 5xx or timed out over a ~20 minute window.

Attached a small sample of request IDs and the short traces we captured (raw-logs-aurora6b-0809.gz). Can you confirm if this is on your side and what the mitigation plan is? We rely on Aurora-6B for embedding-heavy workflows so this is causing queued backpressure for us.

Thanks,
Nate
Sr. Platform Engineer
Acme Energy

Folks — forwarding an external report from Acme (Nate). They observed ~20m of elevated 5xx/timeouts on Aurora-6B. Can we confirm: (1) whether this aligns with internal alerts, (2) immediate mitigation applied, and (3) a brief customer-facing statement I can send asap.

Initial notes from my quick look: I see increased queue depth on a subset of pods and some kernel-level retry logs for the KV cache. Dev, can you validate if we pushed any kernel/runtime patches in the last 24h or if a traffic shift might have hit a degenerate code path? Markus/Marissa — please prep a short external update and routing fallback if needed.

Quoted message below.

Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 12:30:45 -07:00
Subject: Aurora-6B: short update and mitigation steps (INC-2026-0809)

Hi Nate — thanks for the quick flag and the logs. We investigated and identified a transient cache eviction storm that amplified request fanout against a small set of Aurora-6B inference instances, which caused queue saturation and tail timeouts for ~18 minutes starting at 08:50 UTC.

What we did (action taken):
- Immediately re-routed a portion of Aurora-6B traffic to the Aurora-6B-ld variant with a longer KV cache TTL (rolling change at 09:02 UTC).
- Increased autoscaling headroom for the affected GPU pool and evicted problematic cache shards.
- Applied a runtime throttle to large-batch requests to prevent bulk job spikes from starving online inference traffic.

Current status: service returned to nominal for the vast majority of requests by 09:10 UTC. We are keeping an increased monitoring window for 24 hours and will provide a fuller postmortem.

Impact notes: we estimate 4–7% of customer requests to Aurora-6B during the window saw 502/504 or timeouts; your sample aligns with that. We will follow up with a remediation plan and a postmortem document.

Ticket: https://redwood.app/ops/incidents/INC-2026-0809

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as a priority. If you have any immediate questions about the mitigation or need specific request IDs investigated, please reply and we'll pull the traces.

— Markus
VP, Production Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Nate Fisher <nate@acme-energy.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Aurora-6B incident summary & next steps (postmortem attached)

Hi Nate — following up with a concise post-incident summary and corrective actions. Thanks again for the prompt report and the logs you shared; they helped accelerate our correlation.

What happened (summary):
- Root cause: an eviction cascade in the KV-prefetch cache layer on Aurora-6B instances exposed an edge-case in our cache refill path. Under a sustained high-fanout pattern from a small set of large-batch jobs, the runtime initiated rapid cache shard rebinds which briefly overloaded worker queues and produced 502/504 responses.

What we changed (remediations):
- Hotfix deployed (v2.13.4) that ensures backpressure on cache refill and adds a jittered refill schedule to avoid cascades.
- Autoscaling policy updated to add conservative buffer for cache-refill windows and to scale earlier on KV-miss rates.
- Routing policy updated: traffic will gradually shift to Aurora-6B-ld for requests with heavy embedding/batch sizes until we validate stability.
- Alerting: new alert triggers on rapid KV-shard eviction + queue-depth correlation.

Customer impact & credits: we estimate 4–7% of requests experienced errors during the 08:50–09:08 UTC window. We're offering a one-time usage credit for affected time slots; our billing team will reach out if you want the credit applied to the upcoming invoice.

Attached: aurora6b_postmortem_20260811.pdf (detailed timeline, graphs, and sanitized traces). Also linked the incident page: https://redwood.app/ops/incidents/INC-2026-0809.

If you'd like a short technical walk-through with our eng team, we can schedule a 30-minute call this week. Appreciate your patience — we want to ensure this doesn't recur.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
